title: APAC Latency Surge — Handoff & Containment Notes
content:
Summary:
- Time window: 2026-03-27 18:10–19:05 APAC region (UTC+8)
- Impact: elevated 95th/99th token-latency for hosted inference endpoints serving small-batched chat requests. Spike peaked at ~850ms 99th (baseline ~210ms). Error rate stayed low (~0.3% increase) but user-facing timeouts observed in a subset of routes.
- Immediate cause (hypothesis): KV cache thrash + Redis eviction spike on the K/V cache cluster used by prefix caching which caused backend cache misses + downstream backlog. Secondary contributor: one autoscaling anomaly where one dedicated pool misreported available GPUs and routing sent more traffic to a single availability zone.

What I (Maya) did during shift (chronological):
- 18:12 — Alert fired (latency-surge-apac). Pulled SLO dashboard (console/redwood/latency/apac) and the pod-level tail of logs for edge-proxy and cache-proxy.
- 18:15 — Scoped to prefix-caching calls: saw cache hit rate drop from 92% -> 48% across the region at the same time as redis 'eviction' counter jumped.
- 18:20 — Engaged on-call infra (Rohit) via pager and #infra-ops. Started inspecting redis-cluster-03 metrics and memory pressure. Noted one node with 95% memory and high aof rewrite activity.
- 18:26 — Enabled temporary routing-policy: route-apac-fallback (send new sessions to apac-secondary) to bleed load away from the affected AZ. Verified traffic shift (~27% shifted) and tail latency improved to ~420ms.
- 18:33 — Restarted cache-proxy deployment in the affected AZ (kubectl rollout restart deploy/cache-proxy -n inference-apac-az2) to re-establish memory usage pattern and rewarm local caches.
- 18:40 — Deployed faster eviction policy change to Redis (config tweak: maxmemory-policy volatile-lru -> allkeys-lru for cluster-03) as short-term stopgap after discussing risks with infra team.
- 18:47 — Observed cache hit rate recover to ~82% and 99th latency drop to ~260ms for shifted traffic.
- 18:55 — Monitored additional anomalies: a single dedicated-serving-pool reported degraded GPUs (nvml warnings); opened JIRA-SRE-1294 to track hardware/driver investigation.
- 19:05 — Handoff prep: wrote this note and paged next shift.

Commands / snippets I ran (copyable):
- kubectl -n inference-apac-az2 get pods -o wide | grep cache-proxy
- kubectl -n inference-apac-az2 logs deploy/cache-proxy -f --tail=200
- kubectl rollout restart deploy/cache-proxy -n inference-apac-az2
- redis-cli -h redis-03-node-02 info memory | grep used_memory
- redis-cli -h redis-03-node-02 config set maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
- curl -sS -X POST "https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/policies/route-apac-fallback/activate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY"

Observability notes (what to look at in next shift):
- Console dashboards: hosted-api -> per-route latency -> filter by route prefix /chat/small-batch and APAC region. Watch 95th/99th trends.
- Redis cluster-03: memory_used_bytes, eviction_count, instantaneous_ops_per_sec, aof_rewrite_in_progress.
- Serving pool health: gpu_utilization, nvml errors, driver restart counts.
- Router metrics: active_sessions_by_pool, retry_rate_to_secondary, request_queue_depth.
- Traces: sample traces for requests with latency > 600ms to see where time is spent (edge-proxy vs model-serving).

Immediate follow-ups (high priority):
- (P0) Confirm whether redis cluster had a background AOF rewrite at the time (Rohit) — this likely caused CPU and memory spikes on one node. Ticket: JIRA-SRE-1294.
- (P0) Run a post-incident script to capture core dumps/log rotation for the affected GPU host; check nvml driver logs (SRE infra).
- (P1) Evaluate whether cache rewarm is insufficient after restart — add a pre-warm job to rehydrate hot prefixes on restart.
- (P1) Add a short-term alert that combines eviction_count spike + cache hit rate drop so we detect this pattern earlier.

Suggested runbook edits (drafted inline):
- Add section: "Redis memory-pressure triage"
  - Indicators: eviction_count > 100/min AND memory_used_percent > 80% on any node for >2 min.
  - Actions: 1) check for AOF/rewrites (redis INFO); 2) if rewrite in progress, evaluate wait vs restart node; 3) set maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru on cluster as temporary measure; 4) scale out read-replicas if applicable.
- Add a step for controlled cache-proxy restart: ensure new routing policy to shift 20–40% of new sessions to secondary before restart to avoid cold-cache storms.
- Add a 'GPU-host degraded' checklist to runbook for dedicated pools: capture nvml logs, mark host cordoned, evict running shards to avoid tail latency spikes.

Triage notes / unresolved questions (notes-to-self style):
- Why did only one AZ report AOF rewrite? Is there periodic maintenance that lines up with 18:20 local time? Check cloud-ops maintenance calendar.
- Autoscaler misreport: logs show kube-node-metrics-heartbeat missed one cycle at 17:58 — investigate if heartbeat gaps correlate with pool routing decisions.
- Confirm whether any recent deploys touched prefix-cache logic in the last 24h (link to PRs in linked_artifacts if found).

Items assigned / owners: (please add estimates)
- Rohit: investigate redis AOF timeline + mitigation plan (owner). Linked ticket: JIRA-SRE-1294.
- Sofia: add the combined eviction+hitrate alert to observability (owner).
- Maya (me): draft runbook edits and pre-warm job spec; coordinate with infra for safe redis config changes.

Post-incident follow-up meeting proposal:
- Suggested runbook review + postmortem sync: 2026-03-29 09:00 UTC (30–45 min). Attendees: SRE on-call rotation, infra, serving-runtime lead, product-owner for hosted-api. Agenda: root causes, runbook changes, short-term mitigations, longer-term changes (cache architecture).

Quick links / references: 
- SLO dashboard: console.redwood/internal/latency/apac
- Incident pager thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0LATENCY/p18392
- JIRA: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SRE-1294

Notes to incoming on-call (priority checklist):
1) Confirm routing policy state: is route-apac-fallback still active? If yes, consider gradual deactivate only after 2 hours stable.
2) Watch redis eviction_count; if another spike occurs, escalate to infra lead immediately.
3) If 99th latency climbs above 600ms for >10m, re-open pager and consider emergency traffic throttling on non-critical routes.

End of handoff.

-- Maya C. (APAC evening on-call)
